Os filtros escolhem linhas: a linha traz todas as contas não arquivadas do titular, não só as que casaram. Com busca, quem casa pelo próprio nome vem primeiro (nome igual, depois começando pelo termo, depois uma palavra começando pelo termo, depois contendo), e só então quem casou por outro campo ou pelas contas; a ordem escolhida desempata dentro de cada faixa.

delete.description: Apaga a conta de verdade quando nada a referencia; com histórico (emissões, inclusive na lixeira; lotes; períodos; extrato; beneficiários) ela é arquivada: some das listagens e dos seletores, e as emissões antigas continuam mostrando em que conta foram feitas. Os apelidos vão junto nos dois casos.

post.description: Dispara, em segundo plano, o login que descobre o customerKey da conta e o guarda cifrado. Retorna 202 na hora; o painel acompanha pelo estado da sincronização (campo connecting em GET /accounts/{id}/azul-statement), que vira "conectado" no sucesso ou um estado de erro na falha. Após N falhas seguidas a conta é marcada como "precisa de atenção". Uma segunda chamada enquanto um login já está em andamento é recusada com 409.

409.description: Já existe um login em andamento para esta conta

get.description: Concilia o extrato que o coletor sincronizou da Azul (tabela azul_statement_lines) com o que o painel tem da conta, no período que a janela sincronizada cobre. Não há upload — a Azul deixou de subir CSV. Devolve as três listas com o veredito de cada linha e nada é gravado. Crédito sem lote é o achado que importa. Conta sem janela sincronizada devolve uma comparação vazia.

post.description: Fixa o vínculo de uma linha de compra ou acúmulo a um lote da conta, substituindo o vínculo automático (que casa pelos créditos que o lote guardou). O lote precisa ser da própria conta.
post.summary: Vincular manualmente uma linha de entrada a um lote

422.description: Conta sem estoque próprio ou lote não é da conta

delete.description: Apaga o vínculo manual de uma linha de compra ou acúmulo, devolvendo-a ao casamento automático por créditos. A resposta traz como a linha passa a resolver.
delete.summary: Remover o vínculo manual de uma linha de entrada com o lote

post.description: Soma os créditos marcados que compartilham origem e agência num único lote, datado no crédito mais antigo do grupo. O extrato é relido da janela sincronizada e conciliado de novo do zero, então uma seleção que já deixou de ser um crédito sem lote é pulada em vez de duplicar o lançamento. Ao fim, recalcula o custeio da conta.
post.summary: Lançar lotes a partir do extrato sincronizado da Azul

422.description: Conta sem estoque próprio ou seleção grande demais

get.description: Lista as linhas do extrato que o coletor sincronizou da Azul (tabela azul_statement_lines), em ordem de dia, cada resgate/reembolso já vinculado à emissão real do banco quando o localizador bate (ignorando a data, como o lote). Traz o estado da sincronização para o cabeçalho e o período que a janela cobre. Nada é gravado. Conta sem janela sincronizada devolve lista vazia.
get.summary: Extrato sincronizado da Azul, com vínculo de emissões

get.description: Baixa o extrato sincronizado da conta como CSV no mesmo formato que a Azul exportava (Conta, Data, Operação, Localizador, Valor, Origem, Destino, Descrição), em ordem de dia. As quatro operações antigas (Resgate, Reembolso, Acúmulo de voo, Acúmulo de pontos) são reimportáveis; expiração e outros saem rotulados.
get.summary: Exportar o extrato sincronizado da Azul em CSV

parameters.description: Último dia, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, dia de Brasília)

post.description: Fixa o vínculo de um localizador do extrato a uma emissão real da conta, substituindo o vínculo automático. A emissão precisa ser da própria conta. Usado pelo modo de edição da página de extrato.
post.summary: Vincular manualmente uma linha do extrato a uma emissão

delete.description: Apaga o vínculo manual de um localizador, devolvendo-o ao vínculo automático por localizador. A resposta traz como o localizador passa a resolver (o automático, ou nulo se não houver).
delete.summary: Remover o vínculo manual de uma linha do extrato

get.description: Devolve só o "crachá" da sincronização (conectado, conectando + desde quando, último saldo e última sincronização), sem carregar as linhas do extrato. É o que o card da conta consulta em intervalo enquanto um login roda em segundo plano, para saber quando ele terminou sem sobreviver a um F5 travado. Conta nunca sincronizada devolve estado "pending", não erro.
get.summary: Estado da conexão/sincronização da conta Azul

get.description: Retorna as pessoas que já foram emitidas nesta conta, com quantas emissões cada uma tem e quando foi a última. O CPF só aparece mascarado — o número não é armazenado.

post.description: Registra à mão uma pessoa emitida nesta conta — para o caso em que a emissão não está no sistema. Se o CPF for informado, apenas a impressão digital e a máscara são guardadas; o número não.
Descarta o que foi ajustado à mão e recalcula a lista pelas emissões da conta. Admin-only, e sem desfazer.
post.summary: Reconstruir os beneficiários a partir das emissões

delete.description: Apaga um beneficiário e as emissões que ele consumiu nesta conta. Use para quem entrou errado — não para desfazer um cancelamento, já que a vaga usada não volta.

patch.description: Corrige o nome ou informa o CPF de um beneficiário. O CPF é guardado como impressão digital e máscara — o número não fica no banco.

post.description: Move as emissões de um beneficiário para outro e apaga o de origem. É a correção do caso em que a mesma pessoa entrou duas vezes com grafias diferentes.

post.description: Prepara um login na página oficial da LATAM e devolve o endereço para o painel abrir. O operador faz o login (e a verificação, se a LATAM pedir) na própria LATAM; no fim o navegador pergunta se pode abrir o programa instalado no computador, que devolve a resposta ao painel em /latam-connect/callback. O login vale por 15 minutos.

delete.description: Apaga a sessão guardada, deixando a conta como antes de ser conectada. O último saldo lido continua na conta. Reconectar exige um login novo na LATAM.

post.description: Faz o login na Smiles com o login e a senha já salvos na conta. Normalmente a Smiles exige um código de verificação: a resposta traz mfa_required e a lista de canais cadastrados pelo titular (SMS/e-mail), com o destino mascarado. O painel então escolhe um canal em /smiles-connect/challenge e envia os dígitos em /smiles-connect/code. Se a conta não exigir segundo fator, ela já fica conectada.
post.summary: Conectar conta Smiles (primeiro passo do login)

post.description: Devolve o mfa_token e o client id públicos para a extensão executar o POST que o edge recusa a clientes HTTP. O canal escolhido é validado contra os cadastrados na conta, e o destino volta mascarado. A extensão completa em /smiles-connect/challenge/complete.
post.summary: Preparar o desafio da Smiles para o navegador do operador

post.description: Guarda o oob_code devolvido pela extensão e confirma que o código foi enviado, com o canal e o destino mascarado. Depois disso o operador digita os dígitos em /smiles-connect/code, como no caminho normal.

Emissões canceladas ficam fora de todo o volume (contagem, pontos, valor e rollups), em qualquer período — mesmo que o cancelamento tenha ocorrido fora da janela consultada; elas aparecem apenas em cancelled_count e refunded_points, pela data do cancelamento. Emite eventos nomeados (ex: issuance.created, issuance.updated, issuance.cancelled, issuance.deleted, sale.updated) cujo data é um JSON com o id do recurso afetado, além de comentários de heartbeat a cada 25s. O cliente deve usar EventSource, que já reconecta sozinho.
Lucro por lote, acerto entre agências e pendências, por conta e consolidado. Não congela nada — para isso, feche o período.

As emissões canceladas também entram no filtro de data/usuário pela data e pelo usuário do cancelamento (cancelled_at/cancelled_by_id), não só pela criação.

post.description: Cria uma nova emissão. issuer_id usa o usuário autenticado (JWT) se omitido, agency_id usa a agência padrão se omitido, e a emissão sempre nasce com complete=false. Uma venda em aberto (client_id=null, paid=false) é criada na mesma transação. flight_date (YYYY-MM-DD) cria a data de partida da perna de ida principal. account_nickname_id é opcional e, quando informado, precisa pertencer à conta em account_id. issued_on (YYYY-MM-DD) registra a emissão em outro dia — uma que faltava e foi lançada depois; omitido, vale agora.

get.description: Gera uma planilha .xlsx das emissões filtradas. O layout é escolhido por layout: control (padrão) ou legacy. Layout control: planilha manual de controle numa aba única (a emissão cancelada é atribuída a quem cancelou, que é onde a listagem também a mostra), colunas A:O (Nº, Companhia, Localizador, Data do Voo, Passageiro Principal, Origem, Destino, Pontos, Milheiro, Taxa, Total, Conta, Observação, Taxa Resgate, Emissor), as linhas agrupadas em blocos por companhia, o bloco TOTAL DAS CONTAS ao final e, ao lado da tabela, um quadro por conta e companhia com os localizadores e o total de pontos. A coluna Emissor identifica quem fez cada linha, já que todos os emissores ficam na mesma aba. Dentro de cada bloco a ordem é a da listagem (da mais antiga para a mais recente). Aceita os mesmos filtros da listagem (data, programa de fidelidade, cia aérea, conta, agência e emissor). Emissão cancelada no mesmo dia em que foi criada entra pelo líquido (pontos e taxas menos o reembolso); cancelada em outro dia entra só pelo reembolso, negativo. A linha cancelada é destacada em vermelho claro. Layout legacy: a antiga planilha EMISSÕES GERAIS, uma tabela só (B:P) com os totais do modelo, mais a coluna TAXA RESGATE em Q. Nos dois layouts a Taxa Resgate é a taxa que a conta isenta (Azul Diamante Unique) deixou de pagar, em branco nas contas comuns, com o mesmo sinal dos pontos.

Uma linha de estorno cancela a emissão do localizador do mesmo jeito que o botão Cancelar do painel; se ela não existir, é criada e cancelada em seguida, e a resposta conta as duas coisas separadas em cancelled e created_and_cancelled.

get.description: Diz se o bot do WhatsApp, a Traveos e cada integração direta com companhia aérea estão no ar, a partir de sondas que rodam em background (bot a cada 60s, Traveos a cada 120s, cada companhia a cada 10min) somadas ao resultado das buscas reais. Aberta a qualquer usuário autenticado, de propósito: quem trabalha na grid de emissões é quem precisa saber que a vendor caiu. Não devolve o código de pareamento nem o JID do bot — esses continuam só no proxy dev `/bot/*`.
Retorna todos os usuários cadastrados no sistema (sem senhas). Acessível a qualquer usuário autenticado (ex: para popular o combobox de "emissor" em outras telas).

post.description: Cria um novo usuário no sistema. Apenas administradores podem acessar.

403.description: Acesso restrito a administradores; agências e perfil de desenvolvedor só por desenvolvedores

get.description: Retorna os dados de um usuário específico identificado pelo UUID.

put.description: Atualiza os dados de um usuário existente. Todos os campos são opcionais (atualização parcial).

403.description: Acesso restrito a administradores; agências, perfil e contas de desenvolvedor só por desenvolvedores

delete.description: Remove um usuário do sistema via soft delete (marca deleted_at, não apaga fisicamente).

403.description: Acesso restrito a administradores; contas de desenvolvedor só por desenvolvedores

remaining.description:
Remaining is Limit - Used, floored at zero. Zero means the next issuance is the one
that gets the account blocked.

resets_at.description:
ResetsAt is when Used goes back to zero, and only exists for a calendar-year cap: a
rolling window never resets, it expires row by row.

used.description:
Used is the count under the program's counting mode: distinct people for Smiles and
Azul, one per issuance for LATAM.

original_points.description:
OriginalPoints is what the issuance being cancelled is worth, when it is already
in the database. Nil otherwise, where the estorno line is the only figure there is.

partial.description:
Partial says the estorno gives back less than the issuance is worth - one leg of
a round trip, one passenger of a booking. The whole issuance is still cancelled,
because the panel has no half-cancelled state, so this is a warning and not a
refusal: 29 of the workbooks' 108 estornos are like this.

refunded_points.description:
RefundedPoints and RefundedTaxes are the sheet's own figures with the sign
dropped - what lands in issuances.refunded_points / refunded_taxes.

target_issuance_id.description:
TargetIssuanceID is the issuance that will be cancelled when it is already in the
database. Empty for create_and_cancel, and for a locator an earlier row of this
same day is about to create.

cancelled.description:
Cancelled counts the issuances an estorno line cancelled - ones that were already
in the database, whether the panel or an earlier row of this day put them there.

created_and_cancelled.description:
CreatedAndCancelled counts the estorno lines whose issuance had never been
imported: it is created and cancelled in one go, so the day's points still add up
even though the booking was never live in the panel.

registered_aliases.description:
RegisteredAliases counts the account aliases the operator's mappings taught the
system. They make the next day of the same spreadsheet resolve on its own, and
the bot recognise the same word in an EMISSAO.

points_unit.description:
PointsUnit is how the sheet wrote its Pontos column, "raw" or "thousands". The
screen says which reading it used, because getting it wrong is a factor of a
thousand and the panel has nothing to check the points against.

account_label.description:
AccountLabel is the alias as the spreadsheet has it; AccountName is what the
panel will show for the account it resolved to. Both, because the operator is
checking one against the other.

cancellation.description:
Cancellation is set on an estorno line and nil on every other row. The row's own
figures stay positive: what the preview shows is the issuance, and this is what
will be done to it.

notes.description:
Notes are things worth seeing that do not stop the row from being written -
an origin or destination the airports table does not know, a partial estorno.

reason.description: Reason explains a verdict that is not Ok, in the operator's language.

uses.description:
Uses is how many issuances this person accounts for, over the whole history rather
than the current window - the panel shows it as context, not as the cap counter.

azul_connected.description:
AzulConnected is whether a customerKey has been discovered for this account - i.e.
whether the Azul statement sync can read it. The key itself is never returned (it is
json:"-" on the model), so this bit is how the panel knows to offer "Conectar" versus
showing the synced balance. Always false on accounts of other programs.

azul_last_synced_at.description:
AzulLastSyncedAt is when the statement sync last succeeded for this account, so the
card can show "atualizado há…". Null until the first successful sync, or on accounts
with no sync state row.

azul_sync_state.description:
AzulSyncState is the sync's current state (pending, ok, error, inconsistent,
needs_attention, needs_reconnect), so the card can ask for a reconnect without a request
of its own. Null for an account that is not connected or was never synced.

category.description:
Category is "unidentified", "standard" or "injunction" - the Portuguese labels
live on the screen. See data.AccountCategory*.

cpf_usage.description:
CPFUsage is how much of the program's beneficiary cap this account has consumed,
and is null whenever there is no cap to report: an injunction suspends it, an
unidentified account gives no basis to claim one, and a program nobody has
researched has no limit. Null means "render no counter", not "zero".

default_profit_share_percent.description: DefaultProfitSharePercent is the split a new batch of this account starts with.

deleted_at.description:
Only ever non-null on an account reached through a past issuance - the account
list itself never returns archived ones. It is what lets the grid label an old
row with an archived account while keeping it out of the picker.

expected_balance_points.description:
ExpectedBalancePoints is what the costing says the account still has: the batches,
less what was issued. Null on an account that does not own its point inventory -
there is no credit side to it in the panel, so a figure would be derived from half
a history. See inventory.ExpectedBalances.

latam_connected.description:
LatamConnected is whether a LATAM session is stored for this account - i.e. whether its
LATAM Pass balance is being read. Always false on accounts of other programs.

latam_last_synced_at.description: LatamLastSyncedAt is the last successful balance read, for "atualizado há…".

latam_sync_state.description:
LatamSyncState is the read's current state (pending, ok, error, needs_login,
needs_attention), so the card can ask for a new login without a request of its own.

owns_point_inventory.description:
OwnsPointInventory is true on an account whose points cost is derived from its own
batches. The suppliers screen reads it to know the rate is not editable there.

real_balance_points.description:
RealBalancePoints is the last balance read off the airline's page, and
RealBalanceCheckedOn the day it was read. Null until somebody looks.

smiles_connected.description:
SmilesConnected is whether a session is stored for this account - i.e. whether the
Smiles statement sync can read it. The session itself is never returned (it is
json:"-" on the model), so this bit is how the panel knows to offer "Conectar" versus
showing the synced balance. Always false on accounts of other programs.

smiles_last_synced_at.description: SmilesLastSyncedAt is the Smiles twin of AzulLastSyncedAt.

tracks_statement.description:
TracksStatement is true on an account whose statement is read from the airline. The
account card reads it to know whether to offer "Conectar".

waives_redemption_fee.description:
WaivesRedemptionFee is true on an account exempt from the airline's redemption fee -
Azul's Diamante Unique. It is what turns a computed fee into "saved" instead of
"owed" on the issuances made through this account.

answered_by_direct.description:
AnsweredByDirect, AnsweredByTraveos and Unanswered split the syncs by who found the
booking. FellBackToTraveos is the part of AnsweredByTraveos where the airline was
asked first and did not answer - the number that has to reach zero.

direct_average_ms.description: DirectAverageMS is the mean duration of the direct attempts, 0 when there were none.

direct_found.description: The direct integration's own attempts, by outcome.

direct_provider.description:
DirectProvider is the name of the airline's registered integration ("copa"), empty
when none is registered on this server.

recent_failures.description:
RecentFailures are the latest direct attempts that did not find the booking, newest
first, capped.

key.description:
Key is what a manual link is stored under: the locator when the line has one, otherwise a
content signature. The page sends it back to link or unlink this line.

kind.description: Kind is the movement in the panel's terms: redemption|refund|accrual|purchase|expiration|other.

linked_issuance.description:
LinkedIssuance is the resolved issuance (for redemptions/refunds/promotions), or null when
nothing matched. LinkedBatch is the resolved batch (for purchases/accruals), or null. A
line carries at most one of them.

note.description:
Note is the free-text detail parsed out of a non-flight redemption's comment - the hotel,
assist card or product of an Azul Viagens redemption ("Ibis Budget … (20/11 - 22/11)").
Empty for a flight redemption or an Azul pelo Mundo debit, which carry only a code.

occurred_at.description:
OccurredAt is the movement's instant in São Paulo time (RFC 3339), or null on lines synced
before the airline's clock was kept.

points.description: Points carries the airline's own sign (negative when points left the account).

key.description: Key is the first line's link key (the locator), what a manual link is stored under.

points.description: Points is the group's signed total; LineCount how many movements it folds.

points_mismatch.description:
PointsMismatch is true when the linked issuance does not add up: the locator's redemptions
against its points, or its refunds against its refunded points.

routes.description: Routes are the legs in the order they were flown ("CNF→SSA", "SSA→CNF").

connected.description:
Connected is whether a customerKey has been discovered for the account. False means it has
never been connected, so the panel offers "Conectar" rather than a running state.

connecting.description:
Connecting is whether a background connect login is in flight right now. The connect is
asynchronous, so the panel shows "conectando" and polls this until it clears - then Connected
is true (success) or the state carries the failure.

connecting_since.description:
ConnectingSince is when the in-flight login started, so the panel can show the elapsed time
(the login legitimately takes minutes across retries). Null whenever Connecting is false.

consecutive_failures.description:
ConsecutiveFailures is how many rounds (login or read) have failed in a row; it is what
tips the state into needs_attention once it crosses the threshold.

detail.description:
Detail is a short human note for the panel (the last error, or a balance mismatch). Null
on an account that has nothing to report yet.

last_synced_at.description: LastSyncedAt and LastBalancePoints are the last successful read; null until the first one.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is when the state row last changed; null on an account with no row yet.

cancellation_only.description:
CancellationOnly marks the issuance as a row that exists only to carry this
estorno: the booking was made outside the panel, so its points were never miles
issued here and the supplier balance must count the refund alone. Registering the
booking and then cancelling it with twice the points is what this replaces.

cancelled_on.description:
CancelledOn (YYYY-MM-DD) is the day the airline gave the points back, when that is
not today. It is what dates the refund in the costing and in the supplier balance,
so a cancellation recorded a week late still lands in the week it happened.

allocations.description:
Allocations are the sales this payment covers, oldest first. What they do not add
up to is part of the credit.

client_id.description:
ClientID and ClientName say whose payment it is, which the history of several
clients at once has to show on every line.

deleted_at.description: DeletedAt is set on an undone payment, which keeps no allocations.

credit_cents.description: CreditCents is what the active payments brought in and no sale took.

message.example: Pagamentos do cliente listados com sucesso

applied_cents.description: AppliedCents is how much of the amount went into sales; the rest became credit.

client_payment_id.description: ClientPaymentID is the payment just recorded - what the panel's undo deletes.

credit_cents.description: CreditCents is the client's credit after the payment, kept for their next sales.

sale_ids.description: SaleIDs are the sales whose lines changed.

settled_sales.description: SettledSales counts the sales left with nothing to pay.

cpf.description:
The full CPF. It is used to compute a fingerprint and a mask and is then discarded -
the number itself is never written to the database.

used_at.description:
When the issuance happened, which is what decides the window it falls in. Defaults to
now, which is right for someone recording today's issuance.

category.description:
Category decides whether the program's beneficiary cap applies. Omitted means
"unidentified", the honest default for an account nobody has classified.

complete.description: Complete overrides the automatically computed value when provided

default_profit_share_percent.description:
DefaultProfitSharePercent seeds the split on new batches of this account. Each batch
freezes its own copy, so changing this never revises a month already settled.

holder_id.description:
HolderID is required: the panel shows an account as part of its holder's row, so one
without a holder has nowhere to belong. Older rows may still lack it; new ones cannot.

owns_point_inventory.description:
OwnsPointInventory puts the account on the batch costing: its points were bought by
us, so their cost comes from the batches rather than from a rate typed on
/sales/suppliers. Omitted means false, which is every account that existed before
this - and what keeps the costing dormant until an account is deliberately marked.

tracks_statement.description:
TracksStatement turns on reading this account's statement from the airline: connecting
it, the periodic sync and the statement screens. A different question from the flag
above - an account administered for someone else has a statement worth watching and no
inventory to cost. Omitted means false.

waives_redemption_fee.description:
WaivesRedemptionFee marks an account that pays no redemption fee - Azul's Diamante
Unique. Omitted means false, which is what every account paid before this existed.

brand_color.description:
BrandColor is validated as a 6-digit hex colour because it is interpolated
straight into the ticket's CSS - a free-form string there would be a way to
inject style rules into every ticket the airline appears on.

direct_booking_enabled.description:
DirectBookingEnabled turns on this carrier's own endpoint, when one has been
built for it. Independent of TraveosSupported: both on at once is the normal
state while an integration proves itself, with the vendor as the net.

requires_origin.description: RequiresOrigin: the airline identifies a booking by the origin too (GOL, Azul).

amount_cents.description:
AmountCents is in centavos and must be positive: money handed back is recorded on
the sale it belongs to, not spread over a client.

paid_on.description: PaidOn (YYYY-MM-DD) is the day the money moved.

agency_id.description:
AgencyID is the agency the client buys through. Absent means the caller's default
agency, so a panel tab opened before this field existed still creates clients.

account_nickname_id.description:
AccountNicknameID is optional - accounts without a registered alias are still
issuable. When present it must belong to AccountID.

agency_id.description: AgencyID defaults to the agency where is_default=true when omitted.

airline_id.description: AirlineID defaults to the loyalty program's default_airline_id when omitted.

flight_date.description: FlightDate (YYYY-MM-DD) creates the primary outbound flight leg.

issued_on.description:
IssuedOn (YYYY-MM-DD) is the day the issuance happened, when that is not today -
a booking found missing on a statement and recorded afterwards. Absent means now,
which is the truth for everything recorded as it happens.

issuer_id.description: IssuerID defaults to the authenticated (JWT) user when omitted.

passenger_last_name.description:
PassengerLastName is the surname typed for the airline's lookup. Optional: when
absent the lookup falls back to main_passenger_name.

cpf_limit.description:
The beneficiary cap the panel enforces. Nil means nobody has researched this
program's rule, which is not a cap of zero - the accounts screen then shows no
counter at all. See data.CPFLimit* for the values.

redemption_fee_domestic_cents.description:
The redemption fee charged per passenger and per trecho when the ticket is issued
fewer than RedemptionFeeAdvanceDays days before the flight. All three nil means the
program charges no such fee, which is not the same as a fee of zero: nothing is
computed at all. See data.LoyaltyProgram and migration 40.

complete.description: Complete overrides the automatically computed value when provided

origin_id.description:
OriginID is required unless Opening is true - an opening balance was carried
forward, not bought from anybody.

domain.description:
Domain is matched against the link's host, so it carries no scheme and no www:
"voeazul.com.br". A subdomain may have its own row when it needs its own
selectors; otherwise the site's row covers it.

success_pattern.description:
SuccessPattern and FailurePattern are regular expressions matched against what
the site shows after submitting. Empty falls back to the wording built into the
promo service.

wait_seconds.description:
WaitSeconds is how long to let the page settle before reading the form. Single
page apps render the promotion widget after the first paint.

amount_cents.description:
AmountCents is in centavos and may be negative - that is how money handed back to
the client is recorded. Zero is refused: a movement of nothing is only ever a typo.

paid_on.description: PaidOn (YYYY-MM-DD) is the day the money moved, which is what the operator knows.

agency_ids.description:
AgencyIDs are the agencies the new user may see. Only a dev may send it; absent means
none, and it is ignored for a dev, whose role already covers every agency.

granularity.description: Granularity is one of hour, day, week, month.

previous_totals.description:
PreviousTotals is the same window shifted back by its own length, that feeds the
deltas on the stat tiles. Nil when the request was open-ended on either side, since
"the previous period" is undefined without both bounds.

cancelled_count.description:
Cancellations are counted by when they were cancelled, not when the underlying
issuance was created - which is why they are their own fields rather than a
subtraction. There is nothing to subtract: a cancelled issuance never entered
IssuanceCount, Points or AmountCents in the first place, in any window.

checked_at.description:
CheckedAt is when the probe last ran, so the panel can say how stale the
answer is instead of implying it is live.

session.description:
Session is the WhatsApp connection state (connected, pairing,
disconnected) and is only ever set for the bot. A bot process can be up
and still be logged out of WhatsApp, so one field cannot carry both.

state.description:
State is one of: up, down, not_configured, unknown. not_configured means
this server was never given the credentials, which is a different thing
from the dependency being broken.

lines.description:
Lines are the period's bookings and refunds on this batch, in date order, so the
screen can open a batch and show what each figure is made of.

parts.description: Parts are the terms the batch's settlements are added up from.

redemption_fee_saved_cents.description:
RedemptionFeeSavedCents is the redemption fee this batch's bookings did not pay
because the account is exempt (Azul's Diamante Unique). FeeSettlements split it by
the batch's percent, and TotalSettlements net that with the points: the three parts
of the settlement the screen shows.

settlements.description:
Settlements are on the points alone - unchanged from before the redemption fee
entered the closing.

totals.description: Totals is every account added together: the figure actually transferred.

agencies.description:
Agencies is each agency's activity in the period, and Parts the terms of the
settlement merged across batches: the calculation behind total_settlements.

closed_period_id.description:
ClosedPeriodID names the closing that froze this range, so the screen can offer to
reopen it. Null when the range is open.

expected_balance_points.description:
ExpectedBalancePoints is what the costing says the account still has, and
RealBalancePoints what somebody last read off the airline's own page, on
RealBalanceCheckedOn. The two side by side are the only way to tell whether the
batches and the bookings add up to reality - no statement export carries a position.
Real is null until somebody looks. See inventory.ExpectedBalances.

pending_points.description:
PendingPoints is stock that was issued before any batch covering it was entered.
It resolves itself once the missing purchase is recorded.

redemption_fee_saved_cents.description: The period's redemption fee saved, its split, and the split netted with the points.

unsupported_split.description:
UnsupportedSplit warns that this account has more than two partner agencies, which
the single frozen percent cannot express - the settlement figures below are not
reliable, and the screen says so rather than showing them as fact.

redemption_fee_saved_cents.description: RedemptionFeeSavedCents is the redemption fee this agency's bookings did not pay.

occurred_on.description:
OccurredOn (YYYY-MM-DD) is the day the airline charged or returned, which decides
the period the movement is costed in.

taxes_passed_to_client.description: TaxesPassedToClient says the taxes go on the client's bill.

client_amount_cents.description:
ClientAmountCents is what the alteration adds to the sale, negative when the client
gets money back. Worked out here so the panel never has its own copy of the rounding.

position.description:
Position is the entitlement's place in the airline's own list. It decides
which icon the ticket draws - the first is the cabin bag - so the panel
sends it back rather than letting the server renumber.

weight.description:
Weight is null when the airline reports a bare count, which the ticket then
labels by kind instead.

source.description:
Source names the provider that answered - the airline's own integration or
the vendor behind it.

adjustments.description:
Adjustments are the alterations made to the ticket after it was issued, oldest
first. Points, ValueOfTheThousand and Taxes above stay the booking as it was made.

cancellation_only.description:
CancellationOnly says the row exists only to carry an estorno the spreadsheet
recorded for a booking the panel never had. Its points are not miles this agency
issued, so the supplier balance counts its refund and not its booking - which is
what the panel needs in order to explain a cancelled issuance whose points never
show up as issued anywhere.

imported.description:
Imported says the issuance came from the pre-panel spreadsheet. The panel
uses it to stop the automatic Traveos lookup after a single attempt, and the
server uses it to refuse issuing the ticket at the vendor.

issued_on.description:
IssuedOn is created_at as the operator's calendar day, which is what every screen
means by "the day of the issuance". Resolved here rather than in the browser so the
grid and the closing can never disagree about which day a row is on.

redemption_fee_manual.description:
RedemptionFeeManual says an operator typed the amount by hand, which is what stops
the next Traveos sync from recomputing over the correction.

redemption_fee_saved_cents.description:
RedemptionFeeSavedCents is the airline's redemption fee this issuance did not pay,
because the account it was made on is exempt. Null on every ordinary account and
whenever the rule could not be applied (no synced itinerary, or a program with no fee
configured) - which is not the same as zero, and zero is a real answer: the rule ran
and there was no fee to avoid.

It does not take part in what the client owes: it is recorded for control and billed
nowhere. See data.Issuance.

traveos_attempted_at.description:
TraveosAttemptedAt is when the vendor was last asked about this issuance,
whether or not it had the booking. The panel needs the failed lookups too:
it is what tells an imported row that has been looked up and not found from
one that has never been looked up at all.

traveos_synced_at.description:
TraveosSyncedAt separates "complete because Traveos confirmed the itinerary"
from "complete because someone ticked it on the grid". The panel needs the
distinction to know whether a ticket can be rendered at all, and the
timestamp rather than a flag because the operator's real question is how
stale the data is.

traveos_syncing_at.description:
TraveosSyncingAt is set while a pull from Traveos is in flight, so every panel
shows the row as busy and refuses to edit it - not just the one that started
the pull. Already filtered for staleness by the server: a marker left behind
by a process that died mid-pull arrives as null.

seat.description:
Seat is null when the airline never assigned one, which is a real state -
several assign at check-in - and not the same as an empty string.

connected.description: Connected is whether a session is stored for the account.

last_balance_points.description:
LastBalancePoints is the account's real_balance_points: LATAM keeps no balance of its own
in the state, so this is the figure the last read wrote.

row_count.description:
RowCount is how many issuances the day holds, blank template rows and the
operators' own summary tables excluded.

answered_by.description: AnsweredBy is who found the booking in the same sync ("traveos"), empty when nobody did.

message.example: Programas de fidelidade listados com sucesso

cpf_limit.description:
Null when the program's rule has not been researched. The airlines change these
without notice, which is why they are editable rather than only seeded.

deleted_at.description:
Same as AccountResponse.DeletedAt: non-null only on a program reached through
a past issuance, so the grid can label the row without offering the program.

redemption_fee_domestic_cents.description:
Null when the program charges no redemption fee. Same reason as the cap above: the
airlines move these - Azul's launched at 90 days and a price per tier - so they are
editable rather than only seeded.

accounts_merged.description: AccountsMerged are folded into the survivor's account in the same program.

accounts_moved.description: AccountsMoved only change holder: programs the survivor did not have yet.

administered.description: Administered counts the accounts the absorbed person administers, which follow them.

keep_nickname.description:
KeepNickname registers the absorbed holder's name as an alias of the survivor. Omitted
means yes: the duplicate usually exists because that name was never registered, and
leaving it unregistered invites the bot to recreate it.

cost_of_the_thousand.description:
CostOfTheThousand is what a thousand of these points cost, in centavos, kept
fractional because the rate genuinely is: 894172 over 632700 points is 1413,2638.
Display only - the costing never prices a slice by multiplying it.

error.description: Error carries the refusal reason when Resolved is nil.

resolved.description: Resolved is nil when the page offered nothing that looks like an enrolment form.

screenshot_base64.description:
Screenshot is the page as the browser saw it, base64 PNG. It is the whole point
of the dry run: the recipe author sees what the bot would see.

owed_cents.description:
OwedCents is what the client owes over every sale in the filter, when the filter is
one client; zero otherwise.

total.description: Total is how many sales the filter matches, which is how long the panel's list is.

paid_on.description:
PaidOn is a calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD), not an instant: the operator knows the day
the money moved, not the hour. CreatedAt is when the line was typed.

adjustment_cents.description:
AdjustmentCents is what the ticket's alterations add to the price, zero when it was
never altered. The panel badges an altered sale with it.

alteration_day.description:
AlterationDay says the sale is listed because its ticket was altered in the period,
not because it was issued there. On such a row, when everything before the alteration
was already paid, AmountCents and PaidCents describe the alteration alone - what there
is to collect that day. When it was not paid, they stay the whole sale.

amount_cents.description: AmountCents is what the client owes: points/1000 * value_of_the_thousand + taxes.

balance_cents.description:
BalanceCents is what is still missing: AmountCents - PaidCents. Zero or less means
settled, which is exactly what Paid reports.

cancellation_fee_cents.description:
CancellationFeeCents is the airline's cancellation fee on a cancelled sale, which the
client pays: it is what BalanceCents still counts against what was paid. Zero on a
live sale.

cancelled_at.description:
CancelledAt set means the sale was reopened by the issuance being cancelled: money
already collected has to go back, as opposed to simply never having been charged.
There is no "deleted" counterpart - deleting an issuance deletes its sale.

client_payment_cents.description:
ClientPaymentCents is the part of PaidCents that came from the client's lump-sum
payments. Such a sale cannot be switched back to unpaid; the payment is undone in
the client's history instead. ClientPaymentPaidOn (YYYY-MM-DD) is the latest of them.

paid_cents.description:
PaidCents is the sum of the sale's payments, which can exceed AmountCents (the
client overpaid) or go negative (more was handed back than came in).

price_adjustment_cents.description:
PriceAdjustmentCents is what the payments control set above (positive) or below
(negative) the computed price; AmountCents already includes it. ComputedAmountCents is
the price without it, so the screen can say what the sale would have been.

connected.description: Connected is true when the account had no second factor and is already usable.

mfa_required.description:
MFARequired is true when a code is needed. The panel then posts a channel to
/smiles-connect/challenge and the typed digits to /smiles-connect/code.

channel.description:
Channel is where the movement was made ("Web", "APP", "MSR"). It is what tells an
operator's own booking from one the airline generated.

day_balance.description:
DayBalance is what the account held at the end of the day - DERIVED by the sync, because
Smiles reports no such figure. It reads the same as Azul's field and means something
weaker: it is built from these very movements, so it can never contradict them. Shown,
never checked.

key.description:
Key is what a manual link is stored under: the airline's own identifier for the
movement when it has one, otherwise a content signature. The page sends it back to link
or unlink this line.

kind.description: Kind is the movement in the panel's terms: redemption|refund|accrual|purchase|other.

linked_issuance.description:
LinkedIssuance is the resolved issuance (for redemptions/refunds), or null when nothing
matched. LinkedBatch is the resolved batch (for purchases/accruals), or null.

locator.description:
Locator, Origin and Destination describe a flight movement; empty on a plain credit.
The airport codes are IATA straight from the airline - there is no city table here.

points.description: Points carries our sign (negative when miles left the account); the payload is unsigned.

sub_type.description:
SubType is the airline's own sub-classification. "Cancellation" on a credit is the only
way this API spells an estorno.

connected.description:
Connected is whether a session is stored for the account. False means it has never been
connected, or was disconnected, so the panel offers "Conectar".

consecutive_failures.description:
ConsecutiveFailures is how many rounds have failed in a row; it is what tips the state
into needs_attention once it crosses the threshold.

detail.description:
Detail is a short human note for the panel (the last error, or what the operator has to
do about needs_mfa). Null when there is nothing to say.

last_synced_at.description: LastSyncedAt and LastBalancePoints are the last successful read; null until the first one.

state.description:
State is one of pending|ok|error|needs_mfa|needs_attention (see data.SmilesSync*). There
is no "inconsistent" here: Smiles publishes no end-of-day balance to check a window
against, so there is nothing that could disagree.

cost_cents.description:
CostCents is what this credit cost. Zero is a real answer - a club subscription and
flight accrual both arrive for nothing.

funding_agency_id.description: FundingAgencyID is the agency that paid for it.

note.description: Note travels onto the batch, for the operator's own labelling.

statement_points.description:
StatementPoints is what left the account according to the airline, positive, with
the legs of one booking already summed.

verdict.description: Verdict is matched, missing_in_panel, missing_in_statement or amount_differs.

created.description:
Created counts batches, not credits: credits of the same origin and payer are summed
into one batch, so four instalments of the same purchase come back as one.

credits.description:
Credits counts how many statement lines went into them, which is what makes a commit
of twenty accruals into one batch readable instead of alarming.

skipped.description:
Skipped counts selections the reconciliation no longer reports as missing - a batch
entered between the preview and the commit, or the same file submitted twice.

message.example: Lotes lançados a partir do extrato

index.description:
Index identifies the credit within this statement, and is what the commit route
takes. The client never sends the credit's contents back - the file is read and
reconciled again from scratch, so the preview is advice, not contract.

account_number.description:
AccountNumber is the programme's own number for the account, when the file states
it. Advisory: it lets the screen warn that the file may be from another account.

from.description: From and To are the statement's own span, not a window anybody chose.

statement_net_points.description:
StatementNetPoints and PanelNetPoints are the change in balance each side claims.
Neither export states a balance, so agreeing on the change is the only check there
is - and disagreeing means something above was missed.

message.example: Saldos por fornecedor calculados com sucesso

account_count.description: AccountCount is how many accounts fed this row - always 1 when grouped by account.

export_counter.description:
ExportCounter is the administrator's supplier-PDF export count, present only on an
administrator-grouped row - the number lives on the person, not the account.

group_key.description:
GroupKey and GroupLabel identify the row itself, whichever way the caller asked the
view to be grouped. The account fields below stay populated so a client that predates
group_by keeps working; on an administrator-grouped response they describe one of the
administrator's accounts, not the row, and GroupKey is the thing to key on.

issuances.description: Issuances is every line that produced the totals above, in chronological order.

account_id.description:
AccountID and AccountLabel say which account the line came out of. Redundant when the
view is grouped by account and the point of the line when it is grouped by
administrator, where one row mixes several accounts.

adjustment_id.description:
AdjustmentID is set on a line that is an alteration to the ticket rather than the
booking or its cancellation. Such a line is still "issued" (miles charged) or
"refund" (miles given back), so a panel that does not know alterations reads it right.

cancelled_cpf_fee.description:
CancelledCPFFee is the supplier's charge for the CPFs the cancellation burned, in
centavos. Only ever set on the cancellation's refund line, and part of what is paid
for it: the line's amount is the credit plus this fee.

cost_cents.description:
CostCents is the exact amount the points inventory charged this line, present only
on an account that owns its points. It is the sum of the batch slices that paid for
the booking, and the figure the total is built from - CostOfTheThousand beside it is
that same amount rounded to a whole centavo per thousand, for display.

cost_from_inventory.description:
CostFromInventory tells the screen this line's cost came from the batches and must
not be offered for editing. An inventory booking the FIFO has not covered yet is
false here, and its rate is typed like any other.

cost_of_the_thousand.description:
CostOfTheThousand is what the agency pays the administrator per thousand miles, in
centavos. Nil means it has not been agreed yet, which is what makes the payment
summary refuse to generate rather than under-report the debt.

date.description: Date is the issuance's created_at, or its cancelled_at on a refund line.

owns_point_inventory.description:
OwnsPointInventory says the line belongs to an account whose points we bought. Kept
for the panels still running the bundle that locked the field on this alone.

reviewed.description:
Reviewed says somebody already checked this line while reconciling. Both lines of an
issuance that was created and cancelled in the same period carry the same value: the
flag is on the issuance, and the two lines are two views of it.

taxes_included_in_cost.description: TaxesIncludedInCost says whether Taxes is part of what is paid for this line.

providers.description:
Providers is one entry per airline integration that reads the carrier
directly, keyed by the provider's name ("azul", "gol"). Empty until the
first carrier is migrated off the vendor, and the panel shows nothing for
it in that case rather than an alarming blank light.

A map rather than a list because the panel looks providers up by name, and
because which ones exist is decided at boot from the registry rather than
being a fixed set anyone can enumerate here.

is_holder.description:
IsHolder takes the person out of the count: none of the programs charges the account
holder against the cap.

complete.description:
The real balance is no longer editable here: it is owned by the Azul statement sync,
which reads it off the airline and writes accounts.real_balance_points itself (see
internal/azulsync). It stays on AccountResponse for reading. A program without a sync
yet (Smiles) simply has no real balance until its own sync ships.

Complete overrides the automatically recomputed value when provided.

default_profit_share_percent.description:
DefaultProfitSharePercent seeds the split on new batches of this account. Each batch
freezes its own copy, so changing this never revises a month already settled.

owns_point_inventory.description:
OwnsPointInventory puts the account on the batch costing: its points were bought by
us, so their cost comes from the batches rather than from a rate typed on
/sales/suppliers. Omitted means false, which is every account that existed before
this - and what keeps the costing dormant until an account is deliberately marked.

tracks_statement.description:
TracksStatement turns on reading this account's statement from the airline: connecting
it, the periodic sync and the statement screens. A different question from the flag
above - an account administered for someone else has a statement worth watching and no
inventory to cost. Omitted means false.

waives_redemption_fee.description:
WaivesRedemptionFee marks an account that pays no redemption fee - Azul's Diamante
Unique. Changing it does not rewrite what past issuances already recorded: the saving
is stored on the issuance and only moves when that issuance is written again. See
data.Issuance.RedemptionFeeSavedCents.

account_nickname_id.description:
AccountNicknameID is only read when AccountID is also present - the two are
updated as a unit. See UpdateIssuance for why.

flight_date.description: FlightDate (YYYY-MM-DD) upserts the primary outbound flight leg's departure date.

issued_on.description:
IssuedOn (YYYY-MM-DD) moves the issuance to another day. The time of day is kept,
so two rows recorded in the same session keep their order in the FIFO queue.

passenger_last_name.description:
PassengerLastName is the surname typed for the airline's lookup. Optional: when
absent the lookup falls back to main_passenger_name.

redemption_fee_saved_cents.description:
The redemption fee this issuance avoided, in centavos, corrected by hand. A value pins
the correction against the automatic recalculation; an explicit null releases the
issuance back to the rule and recomputes it on the spot.

This field is the reason the handler reads the raw body as well as the struct: for
every other field here an absent key and a JSON null both decode to nil and mean
"leave alone", and that is exactly the distinction the override needs.

status.description:
Status transitions the issuance between incomplete/complete/cancelled. "deleted"
is not a valid value here - it's only reachable via DELETE /issuances/{id}.

cpf_limit.description:
The beneficiary cap the panel enforces. Nil means nobody has researched this
program's rule, which is not a cap of zero - the accounts screen then shows no
counter at all. See data.CPFLimit* for the values.

redemption_fee_domestic_cents.description:
The redemption fee charged per passenger and per trecho when the ticket is issued
fewer than RedemptionFeeAdvanceDays days before the flight. All three nil means the
program charges no such fee, which is not the same as a fee of zero: nothing is
computed at all. See data.LoyaltyProgram and migration 40.

complete.description: Complete overrides the automatically recomputed value when provided

amount_cents.description:
AmountCents sets what the client pays for the sale, in centavos: the total, not the
difference. The server keeps the difference from the computed price, so sending the
computed price back clears it. Refused on a cancelled sale, whose amount is its fee.

note.description:
Note follows client_id's rules: absent leaves it alone, and an explicit null - or an
empty string - clears it.

paid.description:
Paid is the one-click switch. It is translated into the statement: true records a
payment for whatever is missing, false clears the statement. Partial amounts go
through /sales/{id}/payments or, for a lump sum over several sales,
/sales/client-payments.

cancelled_cpf_fee.description:
CancelledCPFFee is what the supplier charges, in centavos, for the CPFs a cancelled
booking burned. Only accepted on cancelled issuances; null clears it.

cost_of_the_thousand.description:
CostOfTheThousand is in centavos. Null clears the rate back to "not agreed yet",
which is what makes the payment summary refuse to generate again.

issuance_ids.description:
IssuanceIDs is required and must not be empty - an UPDATE with no WHERE is not a
reachable state through this endpoint.

reviewed.description:
Reviewed marks these issuances as already checked while reconciling. Unlike the two
terms above it changes no money - it records who has already looked.

taxes_included_in_cost.description: TaxesIncludedInCost says whether the taxes are reimbursed on these issuances.

agency_ids.description:
AgencyIDs replaces the user's agencies when present - an empty list removes them all.
Absent (null) leaves them alone, which is what a panel tab opened before this field
existed keeps sending. Only a dev may send it.

AgencyIDs are the agencies granted to the user. Always empty for a dev: the role
itself means every agency.

data.description: 'omitempty' removes the field from JSON if it's nil
